item.title: 149. Reading the City
item.description: Weird girls, liquid lunches, and marathon readings.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Wetherall
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

This week, get weird at the next Weird Girls event with Luna Luna Magazine, check out the new-to-this-newsletter Pity Party reading series, and enjoy a liquid lunch with Electric Lit. Then this weekend, sign up for the astrologically-minded new book club from Black Spring Books or spend some time at the 400-reader marathon reading of The Power Broker. Lastly, this is on next week but it always sells out, so grab your tickets for the next Tables of Contents while you can!

As ever, get in touch with events I should have on my radar and please share the love with your bookish friends!

Subscribe now

Share

Monday, November 9

LAUNCH | Avni Doshi: The First House

Booker Prize finalist (Burnt Sugar) launches The First House, which “gives us a woman on the edge and a dreadful sense of the horror that lies, not entirely dormant, in the domestic” (Financial Times). In conversation with journalist and critic Elizabeth Winkler. (Doshi’s Manhattan launch is on Wednesday at McNally Jackson).

$10, redeemable in-store; 7-8pm; Books Are Magic Montague, 122 Montague Street, Brooklyn, and livestreamed free

SERIES | Franklin Park Reading Series

Franklin Park welcomes Julián Delgado Lopera (Petend You’re Dead and I Carry You), Nicholas Russell (Observer), M. M. DeVoe (The Boy Who Loved Trees), (The Royal We), and Alexia Nader (The Meaning of Daughter). Hosted by Penina Roth, take a shot at winning the readers’ latest books in the free raffle.

Free; 8-10pm; 766 Franklin Avenue, 618 St Johns Pl, Brooklyn

SERIES | Weird Girls x Luna Luna Magazine

A reading series dedicated to celebrating literary weirdness hosted by Luna Luna Magazine editor and (Goblin Mode). Including readings from (Roxy and Coco), (Animal), (Human/Animal:A Bestiary), (The Miseducation of a 90s Baby), and (Beautiful Garbage), with tarot from Disha Travedi. Come for writing community, cocktails, food, drink, and weirdness.

Free; 7.30pm; SISTERS, 900 Fulton Street, Brooklyn

Tuesday, November 10

LAUNCH | Annie Proulx: Stories

Annie Proulx, the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of The Shipping News, celebrates the launch of Annie Proulx Stories: New and Selected, a landmark collection that gathers together the full breadth of her extraordinary short fiction. In conversation with Michael Cunningham (The Hours).

From $40; 7.30pm; 92nd Street Y, 1395 Lexington Ave, Manhattan, and livestreamed

FUNDRAISER | The 2026 Brooklyn Martini Lunch

Electric Lit’s Martini Lunch, a favorite off-site event at AWP, returns to Brooklyn for the second year. Raise a glass and get a sneak peak at what the future holds for EL, as it goes through a leadership transition. Each guest receives a complimentary gin or vodka martini. This is a liquid lunch hosted at happy hour.

$60; 5.30-7.30pm; Elsa, 136 Atlantic Avenue, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Priyanka Mattoo: How to Be Less Useful

(Bird Milk & Mosquito Bones) discusses How to Be Less Useful: The Joy of Inefficiency, a a potent mix of self-help and memoir about reclaiming pleasure in mid-life. In conversation with The New York Times’ Jessica Grose (Screaming on The Inside). (Mattoo’s Brooklyn launch is on Wednesday at Books Are Magic.)

Free; 8pm; Book Club Bar, 197 East 3rd Street, Manhattan

Wednesday, November 11

SERIES | Stage Break Vol. 08

Stage Break, in which four writers read four original short stories, with three audience members chosen at random to read the story on stage with them. Everyone receives an exclusive zine from the evening. Readers include (Fat Swim), (The Lookback Window), of Tanaïs (Stellar Smoke), and Sara Youngblood Gregory (Dead Boys in Space), hosted, as ever, by .

$11.79; doors 6.30pm; Littlefield, 635 Sackett Street, Brooklyn

SERIES | Pity Party

New to this newsletter is the Pity Party reading series from Pity Party Press, with readers including Helen Georgas (Inventory), (Choose This Now), (Playing Card Divination), and Eleanor C. Whitney (Promote Your Book).

Free; 8pm; Orion Bar, 157 Suydam St, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Kylie Cheung: My Boyfriend, the Superhero

(Playing the Victim) celebrates her fiction debut with My Boyfriend, the Superhero—a “deconstruction of the superhero genre that also doubles as a steamy romance novel” (LitHub)—in conversation with Anna Iovine and Kat Tenbarge.

Free; 8pm; Book Club Bar, 197 East 3rd Street, Manhattan

Thursday, November 12

SERIES | The Parlor

A quarterly, interdisciplinary reading series in Flatbush, organized by Emily Roese, Andrea Abello, and the Brooklyn Artery, this iteration features Stefani Kuo, Hannah Lillith Assadi (Paradiso 17), and Dhari Noel.

Free, but donations encouraged for the writers; 7.30-9.30pm; Brooklyn Artery, 1004 Cortelyou Rd, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Mona Chalabi: Ten Lives

Pulitzer Prize–winning data journalist and artist Mona Chalabi launches Ten Lives—a visually striking exploration of money, and the lack of it, in America told through the lives of ten individuals—with The New Yorker’s Jia Tolentino (Trick Mirror).

$10.89; 7-8pm; First Unitarian Congregational Society in Brooklyn, 119 Pierrepont Street, Brooklyn

PANEL | Modern Families: Expansive Depictions of Love

Leading up to the holidays, P&T Knitwear and PEN America gather Cat Fitzpatrick (The Dinner Party), (Black. Single. Mother.: Real Life Tales of Longing and Belonging), and Joseph Osmundson (Spawning Season: An Experiment in Queer Parenthood) for a conversation about the many ways we build families, find belonging, and care for one another.

$12 or purchase of event book; doors 6:30pm; P&T Knitwear, 180 Orchard Street, Manhattan

WEEKEND-LONG | The Power Broker: A Marathon Reading

Four hundred readers will bring The Power Broker by Robert A. Caro to life in the first-ever marathon reading of the classic New York book on the life of Robert Moses. Starting on Thursday at 7 pm with several notable readers, the reading will continue in 10-minute increments around the clock, with an anticipated Sunday midday conclusion. Tickets are for two-hour slots. Organized by poet Brad Vogel.

Free, with RSVP; from 7pm, Thursday to sometime Sunday; Judgy Baby, 170 Second Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

Friday, November 13

LAUNCH | Gabriel Bump: Don’t Stop Snowing

(Everywhere You Don’t Belong) launches his new novel, Don't Stop Snowing—“a compassionate portrait of a man slogging through ‘academic emotional molasses’ to something like true feeling” (Kirkus)—in conversation with LitHub’s Maris Kreizman (I Want To Burn This Place Down).

Free; 7-8pm; Community Bookstore, 143 7th Avenue, Brooklyn

ONE-OFF | Painting and Poetry

Hosted at the gallery space Hollis Taggart Downtown, writers will read works in celebration of Shuling Guo's exhibition Temple II, paintings which bring the female body, botanical forms, and devotional imagery. The event aims to put writers and artists in conversation, with readers Soje, Sigrid Adamsson, Asha Futterman, Hua Xi, and Shuling Guo. A wine and cheese reception to follow.

Free; 6-9pm; Hollis Taggart Downtown, 109 Norfolk St, Manhattan

LAUNCH | Sarah Haas: Jealousy

Sarah Haas launches Jealousy: A Memoir—an obsessive, propulsive memoir tracing jealousy’s arc through a relationship and investigating our darkest emotional impulses throughout the history of art, myth, photographic technology, and perception—with readings by (Trauma Plot), Courtney Bush (Learning), and (The Surrender of Man). With flash tattoos by King Ave Tattoo.

Free; 10pm; Oberon, 7 Freeman Alley, New Museum, Manhattan

Saturday, November 14

LITMAG | Lampblack Lit Magazine Launch: Issue VI

To celebrate to the launch of Lampblack Lit’s sixth magazine issue head to MoCADA for an evening of readings from (Being), Trinity Battle, and Ola Osaze. With drinks, free zines, and copies of the new magazine.

Free, RSVP to reserve; 7-9pm; Museum of Contemporary African Diasporan Arts (MoCADA) 10 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn

BOOK CLUB | Books in Orbit: Foam with Kate Zambreno

Black Spring Books is launching Books in Orbit, a new monthly book club curated in collaboration with artist and astrologer Caitlin Adams, which will focus on one recent release with a past counterpart to enrich the dialogue between past and present, chosen with the planets in mind. Their inaugural event will discuss Foam by Kate Zambreno with Slow Days, Fast Company by Eve Babitz, and Kate Zambreno will be the special guest.

$10, or free with book purchases; 6.30-7.30pm; Black Spring Books, 672 Driggs Ave, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

Sunday, November 15

READING | An Afternoon with Jodi Picoult

An intimate conversation with Jodi Picoult (My Sister's Keeper) to celebrate her new novel, Hollow Bones. Lingua Franca opens the doors of its Jane Street townhouse for an afternoon of light bites and a discussion with Jodi about her new book and her remarkable career. All proceeds benefit PEN America.

$15; 4pm; Lingua Franca Townhouse · 95 Jane Street, Manhattan

item.title: 148. Reading the City
item.description: November 2 to 8
item.dc:creator: Tyler Wetherall
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

It’s a quiet week in book land—or what have I missed? We have the first ever “reading rave” from Open Book Club, a timely deep dive into 2001: Space Odyssey, as well as a handful of great salons, including First Novel Friday, which I mistakenly ran last week. Alas, my systems are imperfect. Enjoy, and, as ever, please share the love with your bookish friends!

Subscribe now

Share

Monday, November 2

SERIES | Miss Manhattan Non-Fiction Reading Series

The reading series that aims to give non-fiction writers a louder voice in the New York literary scene, November’s Miss Manhattan welcomes (The Stowaway), (Hitler and My Mother-in-Law), photographer Beowulf Sheehan (The Father to the Man: The Last Author Portrait Sitting with Cormac McCarthy), and Evan Silver aka Tiresias, a hybrid writer, director, composer, performer and ritualist. Hosted by Elyssa Maxx Goodman (Glitter and Concrete).

Free; 7.30pm; Niagara, 112 Avenue A, New York

SERIES | #YeahYouWrite

This installment of #YeahYouWrite, hosted by Lisa Amico Kristel and Robin Luce Martin, is themed “#Murder #Madness #Mystery #Mayhem” featuring authors (Devil Inside), Tara Weinstein (The Only Way Out is Through), (The Expats), and (The Brood), alongside literary cocktails, food, an open mic, and more.

Free; 7pm; Someday Bar, 364 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn

BOOK CLUB | Thalia Book Club: Arthur C. Clarke’s 2001: A Space Odyssey

The Thalia Book Club revisits Arthur C. Clarke’s 2001: A Space Odyssey, the classic that imagined what artificial intelligence might look like when it appeared. Marie-Helene Bertino (Exit Zero) leads a panel including Rivka Galchen (Everyone Knows Your Mother Is a Witch), Alice Sola Kim (The Year’s Best Science Fiction and Fantasy), and Joshua Rothman (The New Yorker) in discussing Clarke’s enduring novel about space exploration, the perils of technology, and the limits of human power. With a reading from the novel by Stephen Lang (Avatar).

From $19; 7pm; Symphony Space, 2537 Broadway, Manhattan, and livestreamed

POETRY | “The future exists for the most part in the present”: On Poetry, the Avant-Garde, and the Left

What’s going on in independently published, avant-garde and experimental U.S. poetry today? “The future exists for the most part in the present” is a three-night symposium, starting tonight, from The Poetry Project, aiming to situate poetry in our current social, economic and political conjuncture and to think hard about who’s writing it, who’s reading it, what it’s good for, what’s new and different, and how the contemporary landscape of experimental and avant-garde poetry relates to other creative and liberatory traditions.

$10; 7.30-9.30; St. Mark’s Church, 131 E 10th St, Manhattan

Wednesday, November 4

TALK | Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility and the Art of Adaptation

Following the celebration of Jane Austen’s 250th birthday last year, and on the heels of Georgia Oakley’s new film adaptation of Sense and Sensibility, Francine Prose (Five Weeks in the Country), and join The New Yorker’s Critics at Large cohost Alexandra Schwartz for a conversation about Austen’s first novel—and the seemingly inexhaustible appetite for bringing her work from the page to the screen.

From $35; 7.30pm; 92NY at Redeemer, 150 E 91st, and livestreamed

Thursday, November 5

LAUNCH | Mary Beth Keane: Whale Harbor

Mary Beth Keane (Ask Again, Yes) celebrates the launch of Whale Harbor—a sweeping multi-generational saga inspired by the author’s own family history, following eleven brothers torn apart and set on different paths between Ireland, England, Montana, and New York—in conversation with Cynthia D’Aprix Sweeney (The Nest).

$5, redeemable in-store; 7pm; McNally Jackson Seaport, 4 Fulton St, Manhattan

SERIES | Rally Reading Series

The Rally continues its 10th season with three literary luminaries: Kevin Nguyen (Mỹ Documents); E.Y. Zhao (Underspin); and Aurora Huiza. Hosted by Ryan D. Matthews—it’s the heart of a march in the body of a reading series.

Free; 7-8:30pm; Pete's Candy Store, 709 Lorimer Street, Brooklyn

PANEL | Books & Bites

Chef and cookbook author , Han (Dreamt I Found You), Patricia Park (Re Jane), and Hyeseung Song (Docile) join a panel for a cozy night discussing food motivation in their books, along with some shared autumn eats by Caroline Choe.

Free, with RSVP; 6.30-8pm; Yu and Me Books, 44 Mulberry Street, Manhattan

TALK | Donna Freitas and Sarah Weinman: Wolves of Summer and Without Consent

In two gripping books—one fiction, one true crime— (Wolves of Summer) and (Without Consent) explore the nature of violence against women and girls, and the cultures that allow it to hide in plain sight.

From $35; 7.30pm; 92nd Street Y, 1395 Lexington Ave, Manhattan, and livestreamed

Friday, November 6

LAUNCH | Elena Dudum: They Told Me Back Home Would Be Beautiful

launches her debut book, They Told Me Back Home Would Be Beautiful: A Palestinian Memoir—this “deeply felt memoir of race and history that defies social erasures of the diasporic Palestinian experience” (The Whiting Award Judges Citation) explores ’s transformational journey and evolving relationship to Palestine—in conversation with Kiese Laymon (Heavy: An American Memoir).

$5, redeemable in-store; 7pm; McNally Jackson Seaport, 4 Fulton St, Manhattan

PARTY | Reading Rave

​Inspired by the reading raves taking over Tokyo, the studio is turning into a nightclub for readers. Bring a book you’ve been meaning to finish, sink into a cozy floor cushion, and read under red mood lighting while a DJ plays a live ambient set. ​After an hour of quiet, the room will open into drinks and discussion.

$15, including drinks; 8-10pm; Open Book Club Studio, 80 Bowery Street, Manhattan

SERIES | First Novel Friday

The Center for Fiction’s final First Novel Friday for the year welcomes debut novelists Amber Blaeser-Wardzala (Another Name for Red), Alexia Nader (The Meaning of Daughter), and Nafissa Thompson-Spires (The Four Wives and Five Deaths of Richard Milford). Ayana Mathis (The Unsettled) is the evening’s moderator. Enjoy happy hour in the Members Lounge, followed by a reading and conversation in the auditorium, with cocktails and book signings to close out the night.

From $5; 6-8.15pm; The Center for Fiction, 15 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

TALK | Akbar Shahid Ahmed and Rozina Ali discuss Crossing the Red Line & Seasons of Fury

and Rozina Ali discuss their latest books Crossing the Red Line: Biden, His Advisors, and Israel's War in Gaza and Seasons of Fury: Four Families and the Rise of Islamophobia in America.

$10, redeemable in-store; 7-8pm; Books Are Magic Montague, 122 Montague Street, Brooklyn, and livestreamed free

Saturday, November 7

LIT MAG | Big Score Crossed the Bridge

To celebrate the third issue, Big Score is hosting its first Manhattan event, featuring readers from all three of Big Score's prior issues, with Joshua Furst, , Michael Chang, Matilda Lin Berke, Bo Lewis, and Justin Kamp, alongside some classical guitar. Hosted by editor-in-chief .

Free; 6.30-9.30pm; Nightclub 101, Manhattan

ONE-OFF | Cassettes Salon and I Wish Studios present Toast

Cassettes Salon hosts bilingual (French-English) literary gatherings in New York and in Paris. Cassettes also recently published the first issue of its print magazine. Tonight, in collaboration with I Wish Studios (a Paris-based private dining group), they’re presenting Toast, a communal, multi course dinner party, paired with live readings and an art exhibit. While the dinner is sold out, there’s still space to join for wine, art, and poetry afterwards. Hosted by .

Free; 9.30pm; Bedstuy, Brooklyn address upon RSVP

Sunday, November 8

POETRY | Bad Words

A night of poetry readings. DM Bad Words to sign up to read.

Free; 5pm; Grace & Ruby’s, 134 Kingsland Ave, Brooklyn

item.title: 147. Reading the City
item.description: With launches from Barbara Kingsolver, Joy Harjo, and Lydia Millet, and November's Booking Ahead.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Wetherall
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

This week, I can’t wait to get my hands on Jane Schoenbrun’s debut novel, as well as new work from Lydia Millet and Barbara Kingsolver. Also, the London Review of Books is in town for their now annual lecture; and it’s Halloween, with parties at Book Club Bar and The Twisted Spine, as well as themed reading events from Reading Rhythms. And lastly, paid subscribers scroll down for November’s Booking Ahead.

I’ve received so many requests recently and I’m always sorry to not be able to include them all, or to be able to respond to everyone individually anymore. I do hope everyone’s events are a success.

It’s also this Scorpio’s birthday week, so please go forth and share the love with your bookish friends!

Subscribe now

Share

Monday, October 26

LAUNCH | Joy Harjo: Cloud Runner

BPL Presents welcomes the three-term U.S. Poet Laureate, Joy Harjo, who discusses Cloud Runner, a moving collection about grief, loss, and how art can transform suffering. In conversation with Tracy K. Smith, a Pulitzer Prize-winning poet, memoirist, editor, translator and librettist.

Free, with registration; 7-8.30pm; Central Library 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Jane Schoenbrun: Public Access Afterworld

For anyone else obsessed with Teenage Sex & Death at Camp Miasma they’ll want to get the last few tickets for this one. Award-winning filmmaker Jane Schoenbrun discusses their debut novel Public Access Afterworld—“Reads like a David Mitchell fever dream imagined by somebody working the last Blockbuster on the planet” (Literary Hub)—in conversation with Grace Byron (Herculine).

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 826 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan

LAUNCH | Lydia Millet: Fair Ones

In a great pairing, Lydia Millet (A Children’s Bible) discusses her latest novel Fair Ones—a dialogue-driven, fast-moving double novel following two Brooklyn women in their forties reeling from the sudden and baffling death of their friend—in conversation with Jenny Offill (Weather).

$5, redeemable in-store; 7pm; McNally Jackson Seaport, 4 Fulton St, Manhattan

ONE-OFF | Literary Trivia

Join Liz’s bartender’s Zoe and Jo as they host a night of literary trivia. Reserve a spot for your team of 2 to 4. Prizes announced on the night of for the winning team.

$11.49; 7-8pm; Liz’s Book Bar, 315 Smith Street, Brooklyn

Tuesday, October 27

LAUNCH | Chad Harbach: The Brightness

Founding editor of n+1 Chad Harbach (The Art of Fielding) discusses his new novel The Brightness, following the electric, chaotic, everything-can-happen lives of Pella and her best friend, Irma, as they fumble their way out of sleepy, Midwestern Westish College and into a larger world that will upend their connection and everything they thought they understood about their own place within it. In conversation with Leslie Jamison (Splinters).

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 826 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan

LAUNCH | Devon Halliday: To Stay, To Stay, To Stay

celebrates the release of her book To Stay, To Stay, To Stay—a transcendent debut novel, secrets turn contagious, impulses transform into resolutions, and no one is certain whether they will remain in the confines of their Appalachian college town or step out into the unknown. In conversation with Jennifer Egan (The Candy House).

$10 or purchase of event book; 6.30-8pm; P&T Knitwear, 180 Orchard Street, Manhattan

LAUNCH | Ben Lasman: Magazine

Celebrate the publication of the inaugural title from new Ditmas Park press Parade Ground Books with Ben Lasman’s Magazine—a mordantly funny illumination of the absurdity and precariousness of the twenty-first-century media economy. Ben will be joined in conversation by Jonathan Safran Foer (Everything Is Illuminated). Reception to follow.

Free; 6.30-8pm; Lofty Pigeon Books, 743 Church Avenue Brooklyn

SERIES | The Palace Reading Series

The season finale of this Greenpoint reading series with readers (Amizdel), , (Mother Wound), and . Hosted by and Rita Puskas. 2 for 1 draft specials all night!

Free; 7-9pm; The Greenpoint Palace, 206 Nassau Avenue, Brooklyn

Wednesday, October 28

LAUNCH | Barbara Kingsolver: Partita

Pulitzer-Prize winner Barbara Kingsolver celebrates her newest novel, Partita—the story of a brief, passionate, life-changing love affair, wrapped up in what might be the greatest romance of all: our eternal human longing for art and beauty—in conversation with Amor Towles (Rules of Civility).

$41.37, including book; 7-8pm; St. Ann & the Holy Trinity Church, 157 Montague Street, Brooklyn, and livestreamed free

LECTURE | The 2026 LRB Autumn Lecture in NYC: Lydia Davis on Marcus Aurelius

London Review of Books is coming to NYC with programming running from October 27th to 29th. In this lecture Lydia Davis, the author of eight story collections, as well as two books of essays and a novel, will reflect on some of the concepts of the Stoic philosophers, especially the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius.

$31; 7.30-9pm; The Tishman Auditorium at the New School, 63 5th Ave, Manhattan, and livestreamed

SERIES | Nonfiction Dialogues: Melissa Febos with Leslie Jamison

The Nonfiction Dialogues invites MFA Writing faculty to talk with distinguished nonfiction writers about their work and careers. Tonight, , the national bestselling author of five books, including Girlhood and The Dry Season, joins Associate Professor and author Leslie Jamison (Splinters) in conversation.

Free, registration required; 7.30pm; Dodge Hall, Columbia University School of the Arts, 2960 Broadway, Manhattan

SERIES | Ditmas Lit

Hosted by Sarah Bridgins (Death and Exes), Ditmas Lit welcomes Andrew Colarusso, the owner of Taylor & Co. Books, Margaret Kogan (Steppingstones), Maxim Matusevich (Six Trains of No Return), and Kailee Pedersen (Sacrificial Animals).

Free, with RSVP; 7.30-10.30pm; The Urbane Arts Club, 1016 Beverley Road, Brooklyn

FUNDRAISER | Deborah Pease Prize

Raise a toast to the the 2026 Deborah Pease Prize recipient Kelly Link (Get in Trouble) and celebrate the twentieth anniversary of with an evening of cocktails and conversation.

From $300; 6.30pm; The Century Association, 7 West 43rd Street, Manhattan

ONE-OFF | European Literature Night 2026

The 8th annual European Literature Night, hosted at the Ukrainian Institute of America, brings together fourteen award-winning authors, each from different European countries, who will be celebrating the English translations of their latest works during an evening of performances, readings, and panel discussions moderated by PEN America.

Free, with registration; from 6pm; Ukrainian Institute of America, 2 E 79th St, Manhattan

Thursday, October 29

LAUNCH | Itamar Vieira Junior: Saving the Fire

Itamar Vieira Junior (Crooked Plow) presents Saving the Fire—“Village rumors, religious hypocrisy, and family secrets… Saving the Fire weaves all of that together with histories of colonization that can’t be separated from nation-states and the people who live in them.” (Lit Hub)—in conversation with (No. 10 Doyers Street).

$10, redeemable in-store; 7-8pm; Books Are Magic Montague, 122 Montague Street, Brooklyn, and livestreamed free

Friday, October 30

SERIES | First Novel Friday

The Center for Fiction’s final First Novel Friday for the year welcomes debut novelists Amber Blaeser-Wardzala (Another Name for Red), Alexia Nader (The Meaning of Daughter), and Nafissa Thompson-Spires (The Four Wives and Five Deaths of Richard Milford). Ayana Mathis (The Unsettled) is the evening’s moderator. Enjoy happy hour in the Members Lounge, followed by a reading and conversation in the auditorium, with cocktails and book signings to close out the night.

From $5; 6-8.15pm; The Center for Fiction, 15 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

item.dc:creator: Tyler Wetherall
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

It’s the on-ramp to Halloween this week, with a horror fiction reading from Language Arts at the New Museum, a panel on Asian feminist horror at The Twisted Spine, and the Lower East Side’s 6th annual Halloween Bookstore Crawl. Also, this weekend, Poets House is hosting a day of free workshops, it’s the inaugural RomCon from indie romance favorites 831 Stories, and a handful of tickets are still going for events at The New Yorker Festival.

As ever, get in touch with events I should have on my radar (details on how to submit are here), and please share the love with your bookish friends!

Subscribe now

Share

Monday, October 19

SERIES | Crown Inn Reading Series Poets Night

The Crown Inn Reading Series features poets (SAINT OF), Kate Deimling (Time Traveling), Chanice Hughes-Greenberg, and Kayla Thompson. Hosted by Penina Roth of the Franklin Park Reading Series, Khaholi Bailey (The Miseducation of a 90s Baby), and Crown Inn co-owner Zhenya Kampanets.

Free; 7-9pm; The Crown Inn, 724 Franklin Avenue, Brooklyn

PANEL | How Three Pages Can Change Your Life

P&T Knitwear and PEN America welcome to moderate a panel on how three pages can change your life. Panelists include Stacy Kim (Envy), agent Pronoy Sarkar, Hachette editor Nana Twumasi, Huffington Post editor Noah Michelson, “Modern Love” editor Miya Lee (Tiny Love Stories), and FSG children’s editor Joy Peskin.

$10; 7pm; P&T Knitwear, 180 Orchard Street, Manhattan

SERIES | Wine and Pine

Wine and Pine, a reading series about desire, welcomes writers Kayla Rae Whitaker (Returns & Exchanges), Benedict Nguyễn (Hot Girls With Balls), (of Late To The Party Press series), and (The Original Daughter). Enjoy drink specials and baked goods, and show up in costume for a chance to win a Halloween-themed prize. Hosted by .

Free; 7.30pm; Ten Degrees Bar, 121 St Marks Pl, Manhattan

Tuesday, October 20

SERIES | Les Bleus x The Freya Project

Another special edition of Les Bleus Literary Salon cohosted with The Freya Project, to raise money for ARC Southeast, providing funding and logistical support to ensure Southerners receive safe and compassionate reproductive care including abortion services. Readers at this event include Han (Dreamt I Found You), Koul (Sucker Punch), (Satellite), and writer and interdisciplinary artist Genevieve Sachs. While tickets are free, 100% of all donations will go to ARC Southeast.

Free, with RSVP; 7pm, Berry Park, 4 Berry Street, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Georgi Gospodinov: The Man with Many Names

International Booker Prize-winner Georgi Gospodinov discusses his story collection, The Man With Many Names (translated by Angela Rodel)—“a stunning collection of 40 distinctive and charming stories, mostly set in his native Bulgaria” (Publishers Weekly)—in conversation with Sofi Stambo (People Who Live Alone Talk Too Much). This event is part of the Community in Translation series.

Free; 7-8pm; Community Bookstore, 143 7th Avenue, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | KGB Lit: Issue 27

KGB Bar presents the 27th issue of the KGB Lit Magazine with a reading from the issue’s contributors, including Ashley Dalle; Riley Mac (Ephemeralphilia); and (Wannabeat).

Free; 7-9pm; KGB Red Room, 85 East 4th Street, Manhattan

Wednesday, October 21

SERIES | Best American Short Stories with Viet Thanh Nguyen

Pulitzer Prize–winning novelist and guest editor of The Best American Short Stories 2026, (The Sympathizer) hosts the annual collaboration with Selected Shorts, for an evening of literature in performance. With stories by Nathan Blum, Sigrid Nunez, and Akhil Sharma to be performed by Sanjit De Silva (War Horse, Inventing Anna), Jessica Hecht (Breaking Bad, Eureka Day), and Denis O’Hare (American Horror Story, Here We Are).

From $19; 7pm; Symphony Space, 2537 Broadway, Manhattan, and livestreamed

LAUNCH | Zaina Arafat: Our Arab

Zaina Arafat (You Exist Too Much) celebrates the launch of Our Arab: On Longing, Belonging, and Hope—a poignant, moving essay collection on the longing and hope of living in diaspora and what it means to be Palestinian today—in conversation with Daniel Poppick (The Copywriter).

$10, redeemable in-store; 7-8pm; Books Are Magic Montague, 122 Montague Street, Brooklyn, and livestreamed free

LAUNCH | Alyson DuTemple: Marvelous Freaks of Nature!

presents her debut story collection—honoring the weirdness in all of us, Marvelous Freaks of Nature!, a story terrarium of all of life’s little heart foreclosures—in conversation with Megan Cummins (Atomic Hearts).

Featuring K-Ming Chang, Catherine Dang (What Hunger), (Find Me Where it Ends), and (Chlorine). Chandra Claypool serves as moderator. (K-Ming Chang’s book launch is at Yu & Me Books on October 20th).

Free, with RSVP; 8pm; The Twisted Spine 306 Grand Street Brooklyn

Thursday, October 22

TALK | Ed Park: Three Tenses

BPL Presents welcomes Pulitzer Prize finalist (Same Bed Different Dreams) to discuss Three Tenses: A Transmission from the Nineties, an elegant, iridescent mosaic of autobiographical fragments that form a portrait of a creative life. In conversation with (Grief is for People).

Free, with registration; 7-8.30pm; Central Library 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn

🎃 | Language Arts presents: A Haunting

Fun to check out the New Museum’s new restaurant, Oberon, at this horror fiction reading by . With readings by On The Rag’s , Unprecedented Times author , East Village-based performance artist Dexter the Angel, Celebrity Book Club co-host Lily Marotta, New Waves author Kevin Nguyen, and Substack’s deputy editor . Sponsored by Irregular Hours.

Oberon, New Museum, 7 Freeman Alley, Manhattan

Pulitzer Prize winner Jill Lepore presents her new book The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State—a passionate account of how rule by machine has ravaged the world—in conversation with The New Yorker’s Andrew Marantz.

$11.49; doors, 6.30pm; Old First Reformed Church, 126 7th Avenue, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Doireann Ní Ghríofa: Said the Dead

Poet and essayist Doireann Ní Ghríofa (A Ghost in the Throat) discusses her new book Said the Dead—a time-traversing, form-defying, genre-morphing story of a reader unraveling the legacies of a fabled asylum and the women who haunt its halls—in conversation with (Ordinary Human Failings).

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 826 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan

Celebrating 15 years of ’s reading series, Couplet, this month’s reading features poets Christopher Kondrich (Tread Upon), Thea Matthews (Grime), (The Going Is Forever), and (A Holy Dread).

Spend a day at Poets House writing poetry in a series of free workshops with instructors Megan Fernandes (I Do Everything I’m Told), Wendy Xu (Phrasis), D.S. Waldman (Atria), and Dorothea Lasky (Memory, forthcoming). Each session lasts an hour, and participants can attend one or more sessions. Free with RSVP, $10 donation suggested; 12-6.30pm; Elizabeth Kray Hall, Poets House, 10 River Terrace, Manhattan

Kwon (Exhibit).

item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

It’s October so hail the first spooky season event, with an immersive reading of Poe at his actual house. Also, it’s Banned Books Week, culminating in Let Freedom Read Day on October 10th, with lots of ways to take action to protect the right to read, after a gut-wrenching year of record book bans. Bookshop.org is offering 15% off select banned and challenged books until October 18th. NYPL has a bunch of programming, including a fashion show and giveaways at many branches, as does Brooklyn Public Library, such as hosting Penguin’s Banned Book Wagon, and there’s fundraisers across the city, like this Romance Read-In at Book Club Bar. And, lastly, the great Marlon James rounds out the week at Second Sundays.

As ever, get in touch with events I should have on my radar (details on how to submit are here), and please share the love with your bookish friends!

Subscribe now

Share

Monday, October 5

SERIES | Crown Inn Reading Series

The Crown Inn Reading Series welcomes (Hidden River), , Emily Mathis, Zkara Gaillard, and Jonathan Farrell. Hosted by Penina Roth of the Franklin Park Reading Series, Khaholi Bailey (The Miseducation of a 90s Baby), and Crown Inn co-owner Zhenya Kampanets.

Free; 7-9pm; The Crown Inn, 724 Franklin Avenue, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | August Lamm: You Don’t Need a Smartphone

Writer and visual artist discusses her new book You Don’t Need a Smartphone—in this revelatory manifesto, anti-tech activist August Lamm gives you the courage and confidence to ditch your smartphone once and for all—in conversation with . Lamm’s Brooklyn launch is at Greenlight Bookstore on Tuesday.

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 826 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan

Miss Manhattan Reading Series teams up with , the online magazine of off-center beauty, literature and culture, for their fourth collaboration. Featuring contributors Emily Jean Leibert of The Cut, SL Carroll (The Art of Conjuring), Madison Jamar, and , and hosted by (Glitter and Concrete: A Cultural History of Drag in New York City).

Free; 7.30pm; Niagara, 112 Avenue A, New York

Tuesday, October 6

LAUNCH | David Byrne: Sleeping Beauties

The incomparable creative force that is David Byrne discusses his new book, Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up, an inspiring reckoning with how breakthroughs across the arts and sciences get forgotten, and how they get rediscovered.

From $40, including book, redeemable in-store; 7pm; Riverside Church, 490 Riverside Dr, Manhattan

LAUNCH | Micaiah Johnson: The Unhaunting

Step into the winding corridors and lavish interiors of Abernathy House with Micaiah Johnson (The Space Between Worlds) for the launch of The Unhaunting, a literary horror novel that reimagines the haunted house. In conversation with P. Djèlí Clark (A Master of Djinn).

$10; 7-8.15pm; The Center for Fiction, 15 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

READING | The Cosmopolitan Girl Reading

Join Hagfish to celebrate the reissue of The Cosmopolitan Girl by Rosalyn Drexler, on site at Garth Greenan Gallery’s retrospective of Drexler’s expansive body of work, “My Life Has a Life of Its Own.” Excerpts of Drexler’s work will be read by Rachel Comey, Penny Arcade, Joumana Khatib, Christine Smallwood, and Natasha Stagg. (I’d never heard of this but there are already 135 sign ups so clearly other people have!)

Free, with RSVP; 6pm; Garth Greenan Gallery, 25 Greene St, Manhattan

Cute movie tie-in from the folks at Reading Rhythms. A special reading party to mark the release of Sense and Sensibility, in theaters October 16, in celebration of sisters and best friends, offering a free copies of the book, an exclusive sneak peak of the film, writing prompts, and themed cocktails.

From $25; 6.30-9pm; The Vaux Social, 570 Vanderbilt Ave, Brooklyn

WORKSHOP | How to Write a Non-Fiction Book Proposal

Learn how to write a non-fiction book proposal with literary agent Kate McKean. She will guide you through the industry standard sections of these documents, so you can learn what will work best for your idea and subject matter. This will be an intimate workshop aimed to prepare your work to share with agents and editors.

$32.49; 7-8.30pm; Liz’s Book Bar, 315 Smith Street, Brooklyn

Wednesday, October 7

TALK | Emily Wilson: Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea

Emily Wilson, translator of Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey, discusses her new book, Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea: Journeys Through Ancient Literature, with Slate film critic Dana Stevens.

$27.24; 7pm’; Old First Reformed Church, 729 Carroll Street, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Adam Wilson: Fail Sons

Adam Wilson (Flatscreen) celebrates the launch of Fail Sons—a pair of estranged brothers drive their father’s cryonically frozen body across a divided America to its final resting place in this darkly comic novel about masculinity and grief—a 21st century update of As I Lay Dying. In conversation with (The Ten Year Affair) and Daniel Kolitz.

$10, redeemable in-store; 7-8pm; Books Are Magic Montague, 122 Montague Street, Brooklyn, and livestreamed free

LAUNCH | Imbolo Mbue: Every Story Is a Love Story

Imbolo Mbue (Behold the Dreamers) launches Every Story Is a Love Story—“Wolo’s life is upended when his pregnant wife dies in a car accident. Three years later, he finds unexpected solace in sharing his heartbreak with an unlikely companion: the driver who killed her” (New York Times). In conversation with (Brown Girl Dreaming).

$10; 7-8.15pm; The Center for Fiction, 15 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

LAUNCH | Sherry Turkle: Artificial Intimacy

Sherry Turkle (Reclaiming Conversation) presents Artificial Intimacy:Who We Become When We Talk to Machines—an urgent warning about how our ever-increasing reliance on human-like AI chatbots is eroding our capacity for empathy, caring, and the very qualities that make us human—with Pulitzer Prize-winning New York Times reporter Kate Zernike.

Free; 7.30-8.30pm; Greenlight bookstore, 686 Fulton Street, Brooklyn

SERIES | Happy Pub Day, Volume I

Welcome to a new reading series! The Happy Pub Day honors published essays, articles, and stories that have not yet received their due through this quarterly salon. The inaugural evening features: Meryl Branch-McTiernan (What You Should Worry About), Kate Shannon Jenkins, Noah Rawlings, Gaby Wilson, and Becky Zhang. Hosted by The Writers Room, beer and wine are on the house! Organized by Anna Venarchik, Enzo Escober, and Shaan Sachdev, all writer, editors, and critics themselves.

Free, with RSVP; 7pm; The Writer’s Room, 740 Broadway Suite 702 7th floor, Manhattan

Thursday, October 8

POETRY | Poetry Reading with Tina Chang, Tishani Doshi, Nathalie Handal & Erika Meitner

BPL Presents welcomes four poets with new books. Tina Chang reads from Lion, Tishani Doshi reads from Egrets, While War, Nathalie Handal reads from Roma Roam, and reads from Assembled Audience.

Free, with registration; 7-8pm; Central Library 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn

SERIES | Nonfiction New Salon: Vivian Gornick with Parul Sehgal

A reading by Vivian Gornick followed by a conversation with The New York Times critic Parul Sehgal, for NYU’s New Salon. The event will conclude with a reception/signing.

Free, RSVP required; 7-9pm; Lillian Vernon Creative Writers House, 58 West 10th Street, Manhattan

PANEL | How Fathers Shape Female Identity

This panel features Chris Kraus (I Love Dick); Douglas Rushkoff, media theorist, author and host of Team Human; and Allan Shedlin, founder of the Daddying Film Festival & Forum for a provocative conversation on the lasting influence fathers have on their daughters, from identity and belonging, to body, sexuality, and the ways women come to understand themselves within the world. To accompany the launch of the “Notes from Daughters” group exhibition.

By donation; 6.30pm; Baci Studio, 55 Anchorage Place, Brooklyn

FUNDRAISER | Off Assignment 10th Anniversary Benefit

Celebration of Off Assignment‘s 10th anniversary with readings with contributors and literary lights Lauren Groff (Fates & Furies) and Pico Iyer (The Half Known Life); libations and hors d’oeuvres; a silent auction of author-annotated books; and welcoming company.

$250; 7-10pm; House of the Redeemer, 7 East 95th Street, Manhattan

PARTY | Shabby Doll House Book Party

Join Black Spring Books for the launch of three new books from Shabby Doll House: Hotliners by , Turn to the Stars by , and New Dark: Stories by . With additional readings from (The Island), Jonathan Aprea, and Michelle Lyn King, the editor-in-chief of Joyland magazine. Hosted by Shabby Doll House founder and author (Log Off).

Free; 7-10pm; Black Spring Books, 672 Driggs Avenue, Brooklyn

Friday, October 9

READING | Epiphany’s Fall Reading

Readings from , Nita Noveno (Mud on the Moon), Ileen Park, , and Joana Urtasun (translator of Between Fish Scales) along with good wine and a seat among writing friends.

Free, with RSVP; 7-9pm; Liz’s Book Bar, 315 Smith St, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Patricia Lockwood: Agate Head/Stone Soup

Booker Prize finalist Patricia Lockwood (No One Is Talking About This) discusses her new poetry collection Agate Head/Stone Soup—“A modern word witch.” (The New York Times Book Review)—in conversation with (Herculine).

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 826 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan

PERFORMANCE | An Evening With Edgar

To kick off spooky season, head to The Bronx County Historical Society for an intimate evening inside the historic Edgar Allan Poe Cottage. Experience Poe’s most iconic works—including The Tell-Tale Heart, The Cask of Amontillado, Annabel Lee, and The Raven—performed as dramatic readings within the very walls of his final home. Hosted by actor/writers Natalie Osborne, Meghan Martin, Saturday Lawson, and Kevin Gonzalez.

Free (no RSVP but limited seats); 7.30-8.30pm; Edgar Allan Poe Cottage, 2640 Grand Concourse, Bronx

PARTY | 128 LIT: 4 Years in Print

Join Black Spring Books in celebrating 4 years in print of small press and multimedia project 128 LIT, featuring readings from Tatiana Krasilnikova, M Lin (The Memory Museum), translator Matt Reeck, Chelsea Forgenie, (B-Dragon Suite), and 128 LIT cofounder (Child Boss).

Free; 7.30-10pm; Black Spring Books, 672 Driggs Avenue, Brooklyn

TALK | n+1: Laura Kolbe and Patricia Lockwood in conversation

n+1 hosts a celebration of two new works of poetry: Laura Kolbe’s The Decadent Movement and Patricia Lockwood’s Agate Head/Stone Soup. Lockwood and Kolbe will read from and discuss their work, followed by a party.

Free, with RSVP; 7pm; n+1, 37 Greenpoint Ave, Suite 316, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Big Score No. 3 Launch Party

A party to mark the launch of the third issue of Big Score, featuring readings by Ellen Whiteside, Matilda Lin Berke, Robert Frankel, Diane Mehta (Happier Far), Matt Proctor, Damon Pham, Joshua Chaplinsky, and Cleo Aukland, hosted by editor-in-chief .

Monday, September 28

Min Jin Lee discusses of American Hagwon—a moving and powerful epic of a modern family struggling to educate their children and survive in a fast-changing world circumscribed by global economic shocks—in conversation with Miwa Messer for a live-taping of the Poured Over Podcast, hosted by Barnes & Noble Union Square.

$43.14, including signed copy of book; 7pm; Fifth Avenue Presbyterian Church, Fifth Avenue and 55th Street, Manhattan

(The Secret Lives of Church Ladies) celebrates the launch of The True Confessions of First Lady Freeman—the wife of a popular and powerful megachurch pastor upends her charmed “rags-to-Rolex” life when her secret past comes roaring into the spotlight in this “funny and juicy and sexy and delicious peek behind the pulpit” (Samantha Irby). In conversation with Cleyvis Natera (Neruda on the Park).

$45.09, including book; 6-8pm; Liz’s Book Bar, 315 Smith Street, Brooklyn

Tuesday, September 29

LAUNCH | Hernan Diaz: Ply

Hernan Diaz, the Pulitzer Prize–winning author of Trust, turns to the future with Ply, a novel that examines the place of technology in the American imagination. In conversation with Jennifer Egan (The Candy House).

$10.89; 7pm; First Unitarian Congregational Society in Brooklyn, 119 Pierrepont Street, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Ayad Akhtar: The Radiance

Pulitzer Prize-winning writer Ayad Akhtar discusses The Radiance, which follows a writer, also named Ayad Akhtar, who is nearly killed in a hit-and-run while riding his bike on a country road. He wakes from a coma subtly but utterly changed: the world now floods in with an intensity he has no framework for and can’t switch off. Akhtar is joined in conversation by friend and actor Robert Downey Jr..

$50; 7.30pm; 92nd Street Y, 1395 Lexington Ave, Manhattan, and livestreamed

READ TOGETHER | Stage Break

Stage Break, created and hosted by Mikey Friedman, is the live reading series where audience members join authors on stage to read. This special edition is in collaboration with Astra House Books, featuring Jonathan Woollen (translator of Superstars), Julia Kornberg (The Parties), A.M. Gittlitz (I Want to Believe Posadism, UFOs and Apocalypse Communism), and Monica Datta (Thieving Sun). Enjoy book-themed drinks specials and stick around for the after party on the outdoor patio!

$10; 6-9pm; McNally Jackson Books at BKLYN STUDIOS, 1 Dekalb Ave, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Sarah Blakley Cartwright: Heavy Cream

Sarah Blakley Cartwright (Alice Sadie Celine) discusses her new novel Heavy Cream—abandoned by her mother in New York, sixteen-year-old Geraldine falls under the influence of three women, each seeking to form her in their image—in conversation with New York-based cook, writer, and author .

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 826 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan

LIVE | WORDTheatre’s Author Actor • Series: Fall’s Finest

WORDTheatre takes the contemporary and classic writing from the page to the stage. For their last event of 2026, expect an evening of light bites, performances, and book signings as actors Alfred Molina (Spider-Man), Jason Butler Harner (Ozark), Maggie Siff (Billions), and Brittany Bradford (Julia) step into short stories by authors Louise Marburg (Fancy Meeting You), Naeem Murr (Every Exit Brings You Home), Stephanie Wambugu (Lonely Crowds), and Ron Carlson (Return to Oakpine), all of whom, except Ron, will be present to hear their works brought to life.

From $25; 5.30-8.30pm; The Players, 16 Gramercy Park S., Manhattan

SALON | Friends From New York x Hallie Elizabeth Newton

Book Club Salon was created as a way to bring people together around writers, books and the city, while supporting Housing Works Bookstore. For this evening, founder Heidi Hartwig sits down with Hallie Elizabeth Newton to discuss her debut novel, Agnes Lives!, set in New York City in 2014. All proceeds go to Housing Works.

Free, with RSVP; 6–8pm; Housing Works Bookstore Cafe, 126 Crosby Street, Manhattan

Wednesday, September 30

LAUNCH | Anand Giridharadas: Man in the Mirror

talks to about his new book, Man in the Mirror: Hope, Struggle, and Belonging in an American City, a searching new work of narrative nonfiction about one death in a New York subway car and the uneasy national portrait it revealed.

From $35; 7.30pm; 92nd Street Y, 1395 Lexington Ave, Manhattan, and livestreamed

Thursday, October 1

LAUNCH | Rozina Ali: Seasons of Fury

Rozina Ali, a journalist and contributing writer at New York Times Magazine, discusses Seasons of Fury: Four Families and the Rise of Islamophobia in America—longlisted for the National Book Award, this sweeping narrative history of the U.S. government’s broken compact with its Muslim citizens culminates in the post-9/11 era of mass surveillance and increased violence. Ali is joined by The New Yorker’s Doreen St. Félix.

$5, redeemable in-store; 7-8pm; McNally Jackson Seaport, 4 Fulton St, Manhattan

READING | Claudia Rankine: Triage

BPL Presents welcomes Claudia Rankine (Citizen) to discuss her latest collection, Triage, following the turbulent friendship between two composite characters, the narrator and the theorist, self-identified sisters struggling to define their wounded histories and their shared but separate lives. In conversation with (I'll Tell You When I'm Home).

Free, with registration; 7-8.30pm; Central Library 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Sarah Langan: Trad Wife

(Good Neighbors) discusses her new novel Trad Wife—a chilling tale of a journalist’s descent into horror as she uncovers the dark secrets behind a trad wife influencer, blending suspense with a critique of modern femininity and the manipulative forces of social media—in conversation with horror novelist Victor LaValle (The Changeling).

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 826 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan

PANEL | The New York I Keep: An evening of obsessions, discovery, and a walk outside

Every New Yorker carries a private city. Tonight a panel of writers, thinkers, and deeply opinionated New Yorkers will each speak for five minutes about the one thing they can’t stop loving about this city. Then you’ll briefly step outside together to discover a new obsession before returning to argue about it. Panelists include: Gabrielle Bendiner-Viani (The Cities We Need: Essential Stories of Everyday Places); Moses Gates (Hidden Cities: Travels to the Secret Corners of the World’s Great Metropolises); essayist Philip Lopate; (A Holy Dread); and poet Brad Vogel, with New York City historian moderating.

$10; 6.30-8pm; P&T Knitwear, 180 Orchard Street, Manhattan

Friday, October 2

SERIES | First Novel Friday

On the first Friday of the month, join the Center for Fiction to celebrate and launch a selection of the best debut novels published this month, with (The True Confessions of First Lady Freeman), Bobuq Sayed (No God but Us), and (Blow Yourself Up). (The Original Daughter) is the evening’s moderator. Kick off the evening with a happy hour at the cash bar in the Members Lounge then move to the auditorium for readings and conversation. The party continues with book signings and signature cocktails to round out the night.

$5; 6-9pm; The Center for Fiction, 15 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

WORKSHOP | Book Magic Live

Rise Literary is hosting a one-day writers’ retreat for emerging writers keen to learn more about the path to publication, guided by a great cohort of industry professionals, including founder Kristen McGuiness (Live Through This), Diana Ventimiglia, Lizz Schumer (Biography of a Body), (Maine Characters), and The Cut’s , amongst others.

$199; 10am-4pm; The Chelsea Hotel, 222 W 23rd St, Manhattan

PARTY | Apples: A Fall Festival with Readings

Earth and present readings by a whole bunch of people including Cora Lewis (Information Age), (Foreclosure Gothic), Honor Levy (My First Book), Sellew (Lover Girl), Anika Jade Levy (Flat Earth), Stephanie Wambugu (Lonely Crowds), and (Wanting, forthcoming). Hosted by Myles Zavelo and Olivia Kan-Sperling.

Free; 7pm; 49 Orchard Street, Manhattan

Saturday, October 3

FUNDRAISER | Poetry on the River: A Poets House Benefit

Join Poets House for their annual benefit event: a poetry reading taking place on a sunset ferry cruise down the Hudson River with acclaimed poets Rickey Laurentiis (Death of the First Idea), Ariana Reines (The Rose), and Tracy K. Smith (Such Color). After the reading, enjoy some light hors d’oeuvres and drinks in the company of the poets themselves and other poetry-lovers. All proceeds support Poets House.

From $125; 4.45-7pm; Brookfield Place Ferry Terminal, Manhattan

item.description: It's Brooklyn Book Festival 2026, and there are all the book events and some.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

Brooklyn Book Festival is in full swing and there’s more going on this week than I can list. Want to read poetry on the subway? Or watch tipsy authors go head-to-head in a spelling bee? You can do it! If you’re likewise overwhelmed, or it’s your first time attending, my tactic is to get a paper program from my local indie bookstore and go old school, circling my favorites and making myself an itinerary. Below I’ve listed a couple events I’m excited about, but check out the rest of the program here.

As ever, get in touch with events I should have on my radar (details on how to submit are here), and please share the love with your bookish friends!

Subscribe now

Share

Monday, September 21

SALON | Lit Society: Between Words

Lit Society is partnering with William Morrow books to host a literary salon, Between Words, celebrating R.F. Kuang’s latest book, Taipei Story. The evening explores Asian American identity, language, migration, belonging, and cultural inheritance through literature, conversation, and Taiwanese food and cultural experiences. Ticket price includes the food and cocktails and a copy of Taipei Story, amongst other goodies.

$125; 6.30-9pm; Hue House, 56 E 41st St, Manhattan

Tuesday, September 22

LAUNCH | An Evening with John Green

John Green (The Fault in Our Stars) makes his adult fiction debut with his first novel in nearly a decade. Hollywood, Ending artfully blends a behind-the-scenes Hollywood love story with an unflinching examination of celebrity and the insatiable attention economy. In conversation with Emmy Award-winning journalist Suleika Jaouad (The Book of Alchemy) and presented with Lofty Pigeon Books.

From $60, including book; 7pm; Kings Theatre, 1027 Flatbush Ave, Brooklyn

POETRY | Laura Kolbe: The Decadent Movement

Laura Kolbe (Little Pharma) celebrates her new collection of poetry, The Decadent Movement—a book-length suite of poems that spins backward in time through the early days of parenthood and the preceding nine months of pregnancy—with poet, critic, and translator Yasmine Seale.

Free; 7-8pm; Community Bookstore, 143 7th Avenue, Brooklyn

ONE-OFF | Casual Encoutnersz + On The Rag present Fishtank

A special reading at the surreal, dystopian conceptual fashion popup Fishtank Live. “It’s equal parts literary salon, fashion pop up, and comment on the social media surveillance prison we’ve all created and now are stuck serving life sentences in.” With short readings by: Christina, Jacob Ace, Jet Neptune, Chris Smalls (When the Revolution Comes: A Fight for the Future of the Working Class), Isabela Weeks, Gracie Hadland, Yasemin Kopmaz, Jessica Denzer, Hannah Lillith Assadi (Paradiso 17), Zain Khalid (Brother Alive), Eli Schoop, and special guests.

Free; 7pm; 93 Canal Street, Manhattan

SERIES | Hunter Distinguished Writers Series: Karan Mahajan

Karan Mahajan (Family Planning) discusses The Complex—“A sweeping tale of political machinations, family drama, betrayal and social transformation.” (The New York Times)—in conversation with Megha Majumdar (A Guardian and a Thief). Reception to follow.

Free, RSVP required; 7.30pm; Lang Recital Hall, Hunter North, Room 424, Manhattan

LAUNCH | Ellen Rachlin: Enheduanna’s Song from the Sands

Ellen Rachlin (Permeable Divide) celebrates the release of her debut novel, Enheduanna’s Song from the Sands—a feminist reimagining of the life of the first-ever author mentioned in historical records: the Mesopotamian female poet Enheduanna, who lived around 2300 BCE.

6pm; Barnes & Noble Upper East Side (87th & 3rd), 1550 3rd Avenue, Manhattan

Wednesday, September 23

#BKBF | Crown Heights Lit Night

Three Crown Heights series team up for this Bookends event, with The Franklin Park Reading Series, World Transsexual Forum, and the Crown Inn Reading Series hosting a showcase of fresh poetry and prose from a mix of established and up-and-coming writers: Naima Coster (Take What You Can), Denne Michele Norris (When the Harvest Comes), Misha Holleb (The A–Z of Gender and Sexuality), Simone Reid (Frozen Sea), and Josephine Simple (The New Yorker). Drink specials, mingling, and book raffle!

Free; 7pm; The Crown Inn, 724 Franklin Ave, Brooklyn

PARTY | n+1 Issue 54: Reading and Celebration

Join n+1 at their office for a reading and drinks in celebration of Issue 54: POWER PLAY. Featuring readings by Walker Caplan, Mark Krotov, Leigh Claire La Berge (Fake Work: How I Began to Suspect Capitalism is a Joke), Maria Marchinkoski, and Colin Vanderburg. Readings at 7pm followed by a party with cheap drinks.

$10, including magazine (free for subscribers), RSVP required; 7pm; n+1 office: 37 Greenpoint Ave #316, Brooklyn

#BKBF | Patchwork Literary Salon: LGBTQ Debuts

In a celebration of LGBTQ debut fiction, Patchwork’s welcomes Kim Narby (Saturn Returning), Jonathan Woollen (translator of Superstars), (Hemlock), and R.M. Cress (Dead Boys Club). Plus, thematic drink specials and prizes, with book proceeds going towards the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund..

Free; 7pm; SISTERS, 900 Fulton St., Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Madeline ffitch: Avalon, Rise

Madeline ffitch (Stay and Fight) discusses her new novel, Avalon, Rise—an uproarious, unabashed novel of an Appalachian town, the diverse locals who make it home, an influx of white nationalists trying to take over, and the ways in which the battle brings out our light—with Harriet Clark (The Hill).

Free; 7-8pm; Community Bookstore, 143 7th Avenue, Brooklyn

SERIES | Lit Out Loud Presents: Goodbye To All That

Join Lit Out Loud for a live narration of Joan Didion’s Goodbye to All That, her iconic meditation on falling in and out of love with New York City. Actor William DeMeritt will bring Didion’s words to life, transforming the essay from something you read on the page into something you experience together. Hosted by . BYOB.

Free with RSVP; 7pm; Open Book Club Studio, 80 Bowery, Manhattan

Thursday, September 24

#BKBF | Celebrating Women-Owned Black Bookstores

The Center for Black Literature celebrates women-owned black bookstores, inspired by the NYC Black-Owned Women Book Store Crawl, held in March 2026. Join for an evening of inspiring conversation with representatives from four beloved neighborhood bookstores: Liz's Book Bar; BEM Books & More; Gladys Books & Wine; and Adanne Bookshop.

Free; 6pm; Medgar Evers College (Academic Building 1), 1638 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn

FESTIVAL | Day of Translation

The 7th annual Day of Translation, presented by the Center for the Art of Translation, connects readers of literary translation, literary translators at every stage of their careers, and anyone interested in the movement of ideas among languages, cultures, people, and places. Featuring three free panels from 2 to 6:15 pm. (Alas, the keynote conversation with Odyssey translator Emily Wilson is sold out.)

Free with registration; 2-7pm; Center for Fiction, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

LAUNCH | Amy Fusselman: Cloud Six

Amy Fusselman (The Means) celebrates the release of Cloud Six—this hilarious and moving novel follows a couple forced into unthinkable challenges when, after dying in a plane crash, they find themselves in the lowest tier of heaven—in conversation with Annie-B Parson (The Choreography of Everyday Life).

$10; 6.30-8pm; P&T Knitwear, 180 Orchard Street, Manhattan

Friday, September 25

#BKBF | Gowanus Dawn Reading: Poetry of Edgar Allan Poe

This is the 10th annual Gowanus Dawn Reading! Readers in a canoe flotilla proclaim the poetry of Edgar Allan Poe to an audience on the Carroll Street Bridge over the Gowanus Canal. Poet Brad Vogel and performer Melody Bates lead a lively contingent in a beloved local custom with a spooky twist. If you’re interested in being a reader for this event, contact poetsafloatnyc@gmail.com.

Free; 7:45 am; Carroll Street Bridge over the Gowanus Canal, Brooklyn

#BKBF | National Book Critics Circle Panel Discussion on Literary Criticism

The National Book Critics Circle presents a panel discussion on both the craft of literary criticism and new opportunities for book critics in today’s challenging environment. The conversation will range from practical tips to the art of the review, and will feature Joanna Biggs (Yale Review), Emily Greenhouse (NYRB), Joumana Khatib (NY Times), and Zoë Hu (n+1), moderated by (President, NBCC).

Free, with RSVP; 7-8pm; Community Bookstore, 143 7th Avenue, Brooklyn

#BKBF | 16th Annual Brooklyn Indie Party

Only a few tickets left for this one! Kicking off Brooklyn Book Festival weekend, Greenlight once again hosts a partnership of the Community of Literary Magazines and Presses (CLMP) and 26 of Brooklyn’s best indie book and magazine publishers to throw a party celebrating the spirit of literary independence in the borough. Have a drink, mingle with Brooklyn authors and publishers, discover new works, and enter for a chance to win a gift bag of featured books and magazines.

Free; 7.30pm; Greenlight Bookstore, 686 Fulton St, Brooklyn

ONE-OFF | FLOODLINES: Where cities and oceans meet

FLOODLINES is an evening of music, poetry, science, and conversation about what happens when waters rise and how cities heal. Coinciding with Climate Week NYC, this program asks: whose bodies bear floods, and what does urban health look like in an age of extreme heat, heavier rains, and rising seas? Hosted by Hanif Abdurraqib (There’s Always This Year), with music by Hurray for the Riff Raff and poetry from Eileen Myles (Working Life), the night will feature curator and design theorist Paola Antonelli leading a conversation with leading scientists, filmmakers, architects, and activists, along with libations and installations in the garden and a DJ set by Madame Gandhi.

Free, with RSVP; Pioneer Works, 159 Pioneer Street, Brooklyn

#BKBF | 2026 Brooklyn Public Library Book Prize Shortlist Readings

Brooklyn Public Library hosts its annual reading of BPL Book Prize shortlisted authors for 2026, featuring (The Hollow Half: A Memoir of Bodies and Borders), (Perfect Victims and The Politics of Appeal), Kate Folk (Sky Daddy), Stacy Horn (The Killing Fields of East New York: The First Subprime Mortgage Scandal, a White-Collar Crime Spree, and the Collapse of an American Neighborhood), Emily Hunt Kivel (Dwelling), and Stephanie Wambugu (Lonely Crowds). In discussion with Jessica Harwick, prize judge and BPL librarian. The winners will be in conversation at the Brooklyn Book Festival on Sunday.

Free, with registration; 7-8.30pm; Central Library 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn

FESTIVAL | Literary Fall: Imaginary Worlds

Just what we need this weekend is more bookish goings-on, but Villa Albertine, the French cultural institute, hosts this two-day festival. Friday and Saturday feature sessions on the future of literary translation, new voices in French and Francophone fiction, and the worldwide booms in romantasy and horror, featuring leading French editors publishing in these genres, as well as authors (The Odds of You), (Six Treasures of the Spiral), John Scalzi (The Shattering Peace), and (Dead But Dreaming of Electric Sheep).

Free, registration required; Villa Albertine, Payne Whitney Mansion, 972 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan

Saturday, September 26

#BKBF | Brooklyn Book Festival: Children’s Day

Brooklyn Book Festival’s Children’s Day, where families enjoy a full day of readings, workshops, performances, book signings, and art projects with favorite authors and illustrators, including R.J. Palacio, Bess Kalb, Mahogany L. Browne, Jorge Aguirre, Adam Gidwitz, and dozens more.

Free; 10am-4pm; 209 Joralemon St, Brooklyn

PARTY | dear friend books closing celebration

Join dear friend books to mark their closing weekend, with a day of live music in the garden followed by a DJ dance party. Sunday features a somatic workshop, community portraits, and a final poetry reading.

Free; 2pm-late; dear friend books, 343A Tompkins Ave, Brooklyn

Sunday, September 27

#BKBF | Brooklyn Book Festival: Festival Day

Festival Day! Attend readings, panels and workshops all day, with personal highlights being events with Marlon James and Colson Whitehead, Téa Obreht, Douglas Stuart, Kiran Desai, T Kira Madden, Megha Majumdar, and Courtney Maum. Or just peruse the marketplace with more than 250 independent and major publishers filling the stalls.

Free; 10am-4pm, 209 Joralemon St, Brooklyn, NY 11201

item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

Some of you may have noticed I forgot to paywall the Booking Ahead section in September’s first newsletter. If you enjoyed it, perhaps consider upgrading your subscription ahead of October! Two of the three events I highlighted for this week have already sold out, which I hope shows it offers some value.

Subscribe now

Lots of indie bookstore happenings on Saturday: it’s Strand Day, celebrating the bookstore’s 99th anniversary with 20% off sale across all locations and online, as well as surprise guest readings and signings; Liz’s Book Bar is hosting a Late Summer Sample Sale; and it’s Greenlight Bookstore’s sidewalk sale and book drive in support of Brooklyn Book Bodega. In other news, Brooklyn Public Library has just launched the first ever crafting supplies library. Into it.

This weekend also marks the start of Brooklyn Book Festival’s Bookends events across the city. I’ll do a deeper dive in next week’s newsletter (please share any you’d like me to highlight!) but, in the meantime, check out the lineup here.

As ever, get in touch with events I should have on my radar (details on how to submit are here), and please share the love with your bookish friends!

Share

Monday, September 14

SERIES | Franklin Park Reading Series

Kicking off the Fall season with a multigenre reading featuring Ed Park (Three Tenses), Teddy Wayne (The Au Pair), (Storyknife), Hieu Minh Nguyen (Staying Still), Nita Noveno (Mud on the Moon), and (Any Kind of Known Tomorrow). Mingle with fellow lit enthusiasts, enjoy cheap brews, and get a shot at our readers’ latest books in their free-to-enter raffle. Hosted by Penina Roth.

Free; 8-10pm; 766 Franklin Avenue, 618 St Johns Pl, Brooklyn

SERIES | Muldoon’s Picnic: Laurie Anderson, A.M. Homes, and Sophie Cabot Black

Muldoon’s Picnic—an evening of music, literature, and everything in between, hosted by Pulitzer Prize winner Paul Muldoon (Joy in Service on Rue Tagore) and house band Rogue Oliphant—welcomes the legendary Laurie Anderson for a new musical performance, along with readings from novelist A.M. Homes (The Unfolding) and poet Sophie Cabot Black (Geometry of the Restless Herd).

From $30; 7.30pm; 92nd Street Y, 1395 Lexington Ave, Manhattan, and livestreamed

PANEL | An Evening with Soho Press

Greenlight celebrates the work of New York indie publisher Soho Press with featured local authors Paula Bomer (The Stalker), Binnie Kirshenbaum (Counting Backwards), and Jeanne Thornton (A/S/L). Soho’s Executive Editor Mark Doten, author of the the novel Trump Sky Alpha, moderates the conversation before an audience Q&A. Wine reception to follow.

Free; 7.30-8.30cpm; Greenlight bookstore, 686 Fulton Street, Brooklyn

SERIES | Miss Manhattan Non-Fiction Reading Series

With featured readers Rakesh Satyal (Blue Boy), Tanya Bush (co-founder of and the author of Will This Make You Happy), Christopher Maag, who writes about New York for the New York Times, (Saturn Returning), and Janelle Greco. Hosted by Elyssa Maxx Goodman (Glitter and Concrete).

Free; 7.30pm; Niagara, 112 Avenue A, New York

Tuesday, September 15

LAUNCH | The Art of the Short Story: Lydia Mathis on Desperate Bodies with Roxane Gay

Lydia Mathis launches her debut story collection—set in the American South, Desperate Bodies explores the desire, humor, and horror in the everyday lives of Black women and girls—with writer, professor, and publisher .

$10; 7-8.15pm; The Center for Fiction, 15 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

SERIES | Miradouro Reading Series

Welcoming a new reading series to Book Club Bar Bushwick! For its first installment the Miradouro Reading Series features Henry Koskoff, January Santoso, Sanum Patel, Lydia Liu, and Noah Hale. Hosted by Eric Baker.

Free; 8-9pm; Book Club Bar Bushwick, 380 Troutman Street, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Jodi Picoult: Hollow Bones

(By Any Other Name) discusses her new novel Hollow Bones—a riveting novel about the risks we take to protect the ones we love in a world where crisis is always just around the corner—in conversation with (The View from Lake Como). This event will be hosted in between Third & Fourth Avenue.

$25.22; 7-8pm; The Great Hall, Cooper Union, 7 East 7th Street, Manhattan

Wednesday, September 16

LAUNCH | Rebecca Knight & Julie Buntin: Notes to New Mothers

In search of the book they needed, Rebecca Knight (Hex) and (Famous Men) invited 65 acclaimed writers and artists—Julia Phillips, Kirstin Valdez Quade, Liana Finck, Jenny Slate, Naima Coster, and more—to riff on shared concerns of new motherhood. To celebrate the launch of Notes to New Mothers, Knight and Buntin are joined by actor and stand-up comedian Jenny Slate (Little Weirds).

$10.89; 7.30pm; St. Ann & the Holy Trinity Church, 157 Montague Street, Brooklyn

LAUNCH | Jim Shepard: The Queen of Bad Influences

National Book Award finalist and Story Prize winner Jim Shepard celebrates his new collection, The Queen of Bad Influences—twelve compressed masterworks from this great American writer of catastrophe fiction, in which lives are upended as much by broken hearts as by collapsing dams, hideously mismanaged wars, gargantuan wildfires, and apocalyptic storms—in conversation with Marie-Helene Bertino (Beautyland). Wine reception to follow

Free; 7.30pm; Greenlight bookstore, 686 Fulton Street, Brooklyn

AMA | Ask A Literary Agent Anything

Chat with literary agent and author Kate McKean. She’ll be available to answer any question you might have about the literary and publishing world. And if Kate doesn’t know, she can point you in the right direction.

$11.49; 7-8pm; Liz’s Book Bar, 315 Smith Street, Brooklyn

Thursday, September 17

SERIES | NYU Fiction New Salon: Julie Buntin and T Kira Madden

New Salons feature authors in conversation with NYU Creative Writing Program faculty members. Tonight’s readings are by Julie Buntin (Famous Men) and T Kira Māhealani Madden (Whidbey) followed by a conversation/Q&A with Darin Strauss. The event will conclude with a reception/signing.

Free, RSVP required; 7-9pm; Lillian Vernon Creative Writers House, 58 West 10th Street, Manhattan
SERIES | Pete’s Reading Series

Pete’s is back after summer break with a great lineup: (Pool House), Han (Dreamt I Found You), Joe Osmundson (Spawning Season: An Experiment in Queer Parenting), and Kayla Rae Whitaker (Returns and Exchangesi). Stick around afterward for a seasonal beverage and to get your book(s) signed, with your trusty hosts and .

Free; 7pm; Pete's Candy Store, 709 Lorimer St, Brooklyn

Friday, September 18

FAIR | Empire State Rare Book Fair

The Empire State Rare Book Fair returns with 15 rare book, print and ephemera exhibitors from across the world. Visitors can browse books, prints and ephemera with items to fit all budgets. (Though that might not include the first edition presentation copy of Ian Fleming’s You Only Live Twice going for a tidy £30,000.) On Thursday, there’s a preview night, with $50 tickets granting first access to the books and including drinks. You can reserve tickets in advance or purchase them at the door.

$15; Friday: 12pm–8pm, Saturday: 11am-6pm; Fifth Avenue Presbyterian Church, 7 West 55th Street, Manhattan

SERIES | Words and Music

Hosted by , with a lineup of readers and musicians: Oyé Carr, Cora Lewis, Ash Wu, Nick Dove, and Luke Auden. BYOB.

Free; doors, 8pm; Bushwick, location upon RSVP

RECEPTION | Let the Poets Govern Opening Night

Passes for the second annual New York Black and African Literature Festival have already sold out, but you can still attend the opening night festivities in collaboration with Harlem Stage. “Let the Poets Govern” opens the festival with a performance, conversation and an opening night reception. Featuring Patricia Smith (The Intentions of Thunder: New and Selected Poems), (Dyscalculia: A Love Story of Epic Miscalculation), (Black Girl, Call Home), Yaissa Jiménez (Ritual Papaya), Titilope Sonuga (This Is How We Disappear).

$28.52; 8pm; Harlem Stage, 150 Convent Avenue, Manhattan

Saturday, September 19

FESTIVAL | The Atlantic Festival & The American Reading Crisis

Passes to the three-day long The Atlantic Festival 2026 start at $500, but they have some more accessible programming too, such as this evening at the Brooklyn Public Library, examining the American reading crisis. Atlantic staff writer Rose Horowitch, Brooklyn Public Library president and CEO Linda Johnson, and the author Hilary Leichter (Terrace Story) will explore how to combat the loss of sustained attention and the importance of intellectual curiosity and a shared culture of reading. Then, the author (An American Marriage) will discuss her acclaimed work.

Free, with registration; 7-8pm; BPL, Central Library, 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn

PARTY | Gladys 1-Year Anniversary Party

Happy 1st birthday to Gladys! If you don’t know it yet, Gladys is a Black lesbian bookstore and wine lounge in Bedford-Stuyvesant. Head over for their all-day celebration with books, music, food, and wine.

Free; 12-10pm; Gladys Books & Wine, 306 Malcolm X Boulevard, Brooklyn

FAIR | Brooklyn Books & Booze Author Book Fair

Brooklyn Books & Booze, the monthly reading series at Barrow’s Intense Tasting Room, is hosting its second-ever Author Book Fair, featuring more than 30 small press and indie authors and publishers selling their books, plus panels throughout the day, an agent pitching session, and more.

Free, with RSVP; 11am-5pm, Barrow’s Intense Tasting Room in Industry City, 86 34th Street, Brooklyn

Sunday, September 20

SERIES | Sunday Salon NYC

The Sunday Salon Reading Series returns with “Between Earth and Water,” a reading featuring four writers whose new and recent work explores migration, belonging, the body, and survival across borders and generations. With Alison Kinney (United States of Rejection: A Story of Love, Hate, and Hope), Ed Lin (The Dead Can’t Make a Living), Joseph O. Legaspi (Amphibian: Poems), and Nita Noveno (Mud on the Moon). Hosted by Carissa Chesanek and Wil Turner with music by DJ DubSix.

This week we have launches from Chloe Benjamin, Emma Cline, and Diane Williams, as well as the start of Brooklyn Caribbean Literary Festival.

Award-winning New York Times Magazine journalist Rozina Ali discusses Seasons of Fury: Four Families and the Rise of Islamophobia in America—a sweeping narrative history of the U.S. government’s broken compact with its Muslim citizens, culminating in the post-9/11 era of mass surveillance and increased violence—in conversation with New Yorker staff writer Jonathan Blitzer.

Playwright and novelist Jordan Tannahill (The Listeners) discusses his new novel The Living Realm—in this slim but expansive novel, a British archaeologist living in Berlin begins to see his dead lovers in a cruising forest on the city’s outskirts—in conversation with Emily St. John Mandel (Station Eleven).

Wilbert L. Cooper celebrates the launch of his first book, The Black Shield: An American Memoir of Family and Power—both an epic history and an intimate family story, a startling account of the lives of Black cops in one Midwestern city—in conversation with Emmy Award-winning producer and filmmaker Ugonna Okpalaoka.

item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC. I’ve returned after a much-needed summer break. Highlight: I found a bookstore bar in a Spanish village of just 92 people—respect for their priorities!

With Labor Day coming up, it’s a quiet week in book land, though I am curious to check out the literary dinner series visiting from London and Cake Zine’s weekend-long event on Little Island. It is, however, a massive month for book launches, so I’ve included an expanded Booking Ahead section for September. Marlon James’ launch for The Disappearers and Emily Wilson’s for Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea are, predictably, sold out, but there’s plenty to grab tickets for while you can (Emily St. John Mandel’s launch, for example). Also this month, we have Brooklyn Book Festival bringing pretty much everybody to town. Have a BKBF event? Make sure to let me know! And I hope you all had a restful and suitably bookish August. Til next week - T

item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

An eclectic selection this week as we enter the slow summer season. With that in mind, I’ve decided to make like the French and take August off. I’ll pause paid subscriptions until I’m back in September, but the Booking Ahead section below includes some of the biggest launches of the month. I’m going to use the time to think about some new features for Reading the City, for which I’d love to hear any of your ideas! Wishing you all a joyful summer, take time if you can to rest and read and be well. And I’ll see you the other side!

Monday, July 27

LAUNCH | Signal Hill Issue Three

This is new to me, and bookish adjacent, but I love the idea. Signal Hill is an audio magazine (how is that different from a podcast?), and if you’re curious, like me, they’re having a party to celebrate their third issue, which includes radio docs, archival investigations, audio essays, new fiction, and a sonic tour.

Free; 7pm; Rodeo, 1134 President St, Brooklyn

Tuesday, July 28

LAUNCH | Valeria Luiselli: Beginning Middle End

Valeria Luiselli (Lost Children Archive) launches her new book, Beginning Middle End—a warm and poetic novel set on the island of Sicily during a summer of wild winds, volcanic rumbles, and unexpected tempests—with a masterclass lecture on storytelling, memory, and the ways writing allows us to record the erosion of time. Accompanied by a series of Polaroid photographs and field recordings, this unique event offers a rare glimpse into the ideas that shape a writer’s work.

$10; 7-8.15pm; The Center for Fiction, 15 Lafayette Avenue, Brooklyn, and livestreamed

and Sasha Karbachinskiy of LittlePuss Press, Jules Wernersbach, co-founder of Hive Mind Books, and Professor of Gothic Literature and queer Studies Laura Westengard come together to discuss queer publishing, bookselling, and readership in Brooklyn.

Welcome back to Reading the City, a weekly newsletter of bookish events in NYC.

In bookstore news, this weekend sees the grand opening of the Rabbit Books & Bar, a mother-daughter-founded bookstore bar in the East Village. They’ll be offering free drink samples and limited edition merch July 24th to 26th. Colloff will also appear at the 92NY on Thursday with David Grann (Killers of the Flower Moon).

$10, redeemable in-store; 7-8pm; Books Are Magic Montague, 122 Montague Street, Brooklyn, and livestreamed free

(American Faith) reads from her latest If You Love That Lady—part elegy to the passing of impossible things, part ars poetica to the possibility of remaking, Popa’s third collection explores the inventiveness of longing and its relentless drive, proving that what breaks us open at last reveals us to ourselves.

Free; 6-7.30pm; The Corner Bookstore, 1313 Madison Avenue, Manhattan

$30, including book; 7-8.30pm; McNally Jackson Books at BKLYN STUDIOS, 1 Dekalb Ave., Brooklyn

$10; 7-8pm; Strand Book Store, 828 Broadway 3rd Floor, Rare Book Room, Manhattan
